records.source: וַֽיהוָ֛ה פָּקַ֥ד אֶת־שָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמָ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה לְשָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And YHWH visited Sarah as he had said, and did YHWH to Sarah as he had spoken.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} took note of Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} carried out for Sarah what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} visited Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did to Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came to help Sarah, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said. He kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise to her.

decisions.choice: visited (paqad): came to act on her behalf
decisions.reason: When God 'visits' someone he turns his attention to them and acts, in blessing or in judgment. The same verb is used when God gives Hannah children (1 Samuel 2:21) and when Joseph says God will come to Israel's aid (50:24).

decisions.choice: as he had said: the promise of 17:19-21 and 18:10-14
decisions.reason: The words are repeated twice over: what God said, he did. The son promised for 'this time next year' (17:21; 18:14) is born.

records.source: וַתַּהַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And conceived and bore Sarah to Abraham a son for his old age, at the appointed time which had spoken to him God.
pieces: Sarah conceived, and when Abraham was old she gave him a son, at the set time God had told him of.

L.2: And Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.

R.2: Sarah became pregnant and had a baby boy, even though Abraham was very old. It happened at the exact time God had said it would.

decisions.choice: the appointed time: the time God had set
decisions.reason: The word (mo'ed) is the one used in 17:21 and 18:14: 'at the appointed time I will return to you'. God kept his own schedule.

decisions.choice: his old age
decisions.reason: Abraham is 100 (verse 5) and Sarah ninety (17:17). The birth is beyond what nature allows, as Sarah herself had said (18:11-12).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת־שֶׁם־בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד־ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה־לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And called Abraham the name of his son who was born to him, whom bore to him Sarah, Isaac.
pieces: Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son who had been born to him, the son Sarah bore him.

L.3: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.

R.3: Abraham named the baby Isaac, as God had told him to.

decisions.choice: Isaac: 'he laughs'
decisions.reason: The name (Yitschaq) means 'he laughs'. Abraham laughed at the promise (17:17), and Sarah did too (18:12-15); God chose the name (17:19). In verses 6 and 9 the word for laughter comes back.

decisions.choice: as God had told him to
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that God gave the name (17:19).

records.source: וַיָּ֤מָל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And circumcised Abraham Isaac his son [as] a son of eight days, as had commanded him God.
pieces: Abraham circumcised his son Isaac on the eighth day after his birth, following God's command.

L.4: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.

R.4: When Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him. God had told him to do this.

decisions.choice: eight days old: the sign of the covenant
decisions.reason: God had commanded that every boy be circumcised on the eighth day as the sign of his covenant (17:10-12). Isaac is the first child to receive it at the age the command set.

records.source: וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם בֶּן־מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֥ק בְּנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Abraham [was] a son of a hundred years when was born to him Isaac his son.
pieces: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.

L.5: And Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac his son was born to him.

R.5: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.

decisions.choice: 100 years old: twenty-five years of waiting
decisions.reason: Abraham was seventy-five when God first promised to make him a great nation (12:2-4). The son of the promise comes twenty-five years later.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שָׂרָ֔ה צְחֹ֕ק עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים כָּל־הַשֹּׁמֵ֖עַ יִֽצְחַק־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Sarah, laughter has made for me God; everyone who hears will laugh for me.
pieces: Sarah said, "God has given me reason to laugh, and all who hear of it will share my laughter."

L.6: And Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me."

R.6: Sarah said, "God has made me laugh with joy! Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."

decisions.choice: laughter (tsechoq): the name Isaac
decisions.reason: The word is the root of Isaac's name. Sarah's laughter of disbelief (18:12) has become the laughter of joy.

decisions.choice: laugh with me: or laugh at me
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that people will rejoice with Sarah, or that they will laugh at an old woman with a baby. The joy of the verse makes the first more likely; Sarah may also mean both.

records.source: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֤י מִלֵּל֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם הֵינִ֥יקָה בָנִ֖ים שָׂרָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי בֵ֖ן לִזְקֻנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And she said, who would have said to Abraham, Sarah has nursed children? For I have borne a son for his old age.
pieces: She went on, "Who would have dared to tell Abraham, 'Sarah will be nursing babies'? But now, when he is old, I have borne him a son!"

L.7: And she said, "Who would have said to Abraham, 'Sarah will nurse children'? Yet I have borne [him] a son in his old age."

R.7: She also said, "No one would have dreamed of telling Abraham that Sarah would ever nurse a baby. But I have had a son for him, even though he is old!"

decisions.choice: would have said (millel): a poetic word
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and belongs to poetry. Sarah's words are a little song of wonder, like Hannah's (1 Samuel 2:1-10).

decisions.choice: nurse children: plural for one son
decisions.reason: The plural states the general idea: Sarah a nursing mother at all. Only one son is meant.

records.source: וַיִּגְדַּ֥ל הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיִּגָּמַ֑ל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And grew the child and was weaned, and made Abraham a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
pieces: The boy grew older, and Abraham celebrated the day of his weaning with a large feast.

L.8: And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.

R.8: Isaac grew. When he was old enough to stop nursing, Abraham gave a big party to celebrate.

decisions.choice: weaned: two or three years old
decisions.reason: Children were nursed much longer than today, often for two or three years (1 Samuel 1:22-24; 2 Maccabees 7:27). Surviving early childhood was a reason to celebrate.

records.source: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶֽת־בֶּן־הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם מְצַחֵֽק׃
records.gloss: And saw Sarah the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
pieces: Then Sarah saw the son that Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham poking fun.

L.9: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.

R.9: Sarah saw Ishmael mocking Isaac. Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, the woman from Egypt.

decisions.choice: laughing (metsaheq): mocking, or playing
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of 'laugh', the root of Isaac's name once more. It can mean to laugh, to play, or to make fun of (19:14; 39:14). Sarah's reaction suggests mockery, and Galatians 4:29 speaks of the son of the slave woman persecuting the son of the promise. Others read it as harmless play that showed Sarah the son of the slave on equal terms with Isaac.

decisions.choice: laughing: the Septuagint adds 'with Isaac her son'
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate read 'playing with Isaac her son'. The Hebrew text, followed here, has no object.

decisions.choice: the son of Hagar: Ishmael is not named
decisions.reason: In this chapter Ishmael is never named; he is 'the son of Hagar', 'the son of the slave woman', 'the boy'. The silence keeps the story's focus on how Sarah and Abraham see him. His name, 'God hears', is echoed when God hears him (verse 17).

decisions.choice: Ishmael ... of Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable names the boy and supplies the object of the mocking. The object is implied by Sarah's reply (verse 10) but not stated in the Hebrew (m1, m2).

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת־בְּנָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן־הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם־בְּנִ֖י עִם־יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And she said to Abraham, drive out this slave woman and her son, for will not inherit [the] son of this slave woman with my son, with Isaac.
pieces: and she told Abraham, "Send this slave woman and her boy away! No son of this slave is going to be an heir alongside my son Isaac."

L.10: And she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son, with Isaac."

R.10: She said to Abraham, "Make this slave woman and her son leave! Her son must not get any share of what is yours when you die. It is all for my son Isaac."

decisions.choice: drive out (garesh): expel for good
decisions.reason: The verb is used for God driving the man from the garden (3:24) and for divorce (Leviticus 21:7). Sarah demands a permanent break.

decisions.choice: this slave woman (amah): Sarah does not use her name
decisions.reason: Sarah speaks of 'this slave woman' and 'her son', never Hagar or Ishmael. The word amah means a female slave, like shifchah in 16:1.

decisions.choice: shall not be heir with my son: the firstborn's share
decisions.reason: Ishmael was Abraham's firstborn. A son born to a slave woman could be counted as an heir, which is why Sarah wants him sent away. Later law protected a firstborn son from being passed over (Deuteronomy 21:15-17).

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: Sarah's demand turns on Hagar's son being a slave's son, not an heir beside the free woman's son (m3; Galatians 4:30).

records.source: וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֥ת בְּנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was evil the matter exceedingly in [the] eyes of Abraham on account of his son.
pieces: This grieved Abraham deeply, since it was his own son at stake.

L.11: And the matter was very evil in the eyes of Abraham on account of his son.

R.11: This troubled Abraham greatly. After all, Ishmael was his son too.

decisions.choice: very evil in his eyes: deeply distressing to him
decisions.reason: 'Evil in the eyes of' means displeasing, distressing. Abraham loved Ishmael (17:18).

decisions.choice: Ishmael
decisions.reason: Readable names the son so the reader knows which son is meant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֗ם אַל־יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ עַל־הַנַּ֣עַר וְעַל־אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֛יךָ שָׂרָ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלָ֑הּ כִּ֣י בְיִצְחָ֔ק יִקָּרֵ֥א לְךָ֖ זָֽרַע׃
records.gloss: And said God to Abraham, let it not be evil in your eyes on account of the lad and on account of your slave woman; all that says to you Sarah, listen to her voice, for in Isaac will be called to you offspring.
pieces: But God told Abraham, "Do not be troubled about the boy and your servant. Do as Sarah says, in everything. The descendants who will carry your name will come through Isaac.

L.12: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let it be evil in your eyes on account of the boy and on account of your slave woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac offspring shall be named for you.

R.12: God said to Abraham, "Do not be upset about the boy and your servant. Do what Sarah tells you. The descendants I promised you will come through Isaac.

decisions.choice: through Isaac offspring shall be named for you: Isaac carries the promise
decisions.reason: The offspring who will be called Abraham's, in the sense of the promise, will be counted through Isaac. Paul quotes the words in Romans 9:7, and Hebrews 11:18 recalls them in speaking of Abraham's test in chapter 22.

decisions.choice: listen to her voice: God sides with Sarah's demand, for his own reasons
decisions.reason: God tells Abraham to do what Sarah says, but gives his own reason and his own promise for Ishmael (verse 13). Earlier, listening to Sarah's voice had led to trouble (16:2).

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in this translation, zera is 'offspring' in Literal and 'descendants' in Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וְגַ֥ם אֶת־בֶּן־הָאָמָ֖ה לְג֣וֹי אֲשִׂימֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י זַרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And also the son of the slave woman into a nation I will make him, for your offspring [is] he.
pieces: But I will make the slave woman's son into a nation as well, because he too is your child."

L.13: And also the son of the slave woman I will make into a nation, for he is your offspring."

R.13: I will make a nation from the slave woman's son too, because he is also your son."

decisions.choice: I will make him a nation: a promise for Ishmael
decisions.reason: God repeats his promise to Hagar (16:10) and to Abraham (17:20). Ishmael is sent away, but not abandoned; for Abraham's sake he too has a future.

decisions.choice: your child (B), your son (R)
decisions.reason: Zera here means one person, Ishmael, so Balanced and Readable say 'child' or 'son' rather than the plural 'descendants'.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as in verse 10: the phrase marks Ishmael as a slave's son, set against Isaac the free woman's son and heir (Galatians 4:22-23), so the style guide keeps the word.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֣ם׀בַּבֹּ֡קֶר וַיִּֽקַּֽח־לֶחֶם֩ וְחֵ֨מַת מַ֜יִם וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־הָ֠גָר שָׂ֧ם עַל־שִׁכְמָ֛הּ וְאֶת־הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֑הָ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ וַתֵּ֔תַע בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃
records.gloss: And rose early Abraham in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave [them] to Hagar, putting [them] on her shoulder, and the boy, and sent her away; and she went and wandered in [the] wilderness of Beersheba.
pieces: Abraham was up at dawn. He took food and a skin of water and handed them to Hagar, setting them on her shoulder; he handed over the boy too, and sent her away. She left and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.

L.14: So Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave [them] to Hagar, putting [them] on her shoulder, and the boy, and he sent her away. And she went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.

R.14: Abraham got up early the next morning. He gave Hagar some food and a leather bag full of water. He put them on her shoulder and sent her away with her son. She went off and wandered in the desert near Beersheba.

decisions.choice: a skin of water: a leather water bag
decisions.reason: Water was carried in a bag made from a goatskin. One skin would not last long in the desert.

decisions.choice: putting them on her shoulder, and the boy: who carries what
alternatives: putting them and the boy on her shoulder
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read as Abraham putting the food and water on her shoulder and giving her the boy, or as putting the boy too on her shoulder. Ishmael was about sixteen (16:16; 21:5, 8), which makes the first reading more likely; the second would picture him as a child.

decisions.choice: sent her away ... wandered
decisions.reason: 'Sent away' (shillach) is the word used for releasing a slave or divorcing a wife (Deuteronomy 15:13; 24:1). 'Wandered' is the word Abraham used of his own travels (20:13), and can also mean to lose one's way.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Beersheba: the dry land around Beersheba
decisions.reason: The place gets its name later in this chapter (verse 31); the narrator uses the name the reader knows.

records.source: וַיִּכְל֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מִן־הַחֵ֑מֶת וַתַּשְׁלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־הַיֶּ֔לֶד תַּ֖חַת אַחַ֥ד הַשִּׂיחִֽם׃
records.gloss: And were finished the water from the skin, and she threw the boy under one of the bushes.
pieces: Once the skin had no water left, she laid the boy down under one of the shrubs.

L.15: And the water in the skin was used up, and she cast the boy under one of the bushes.

R.15: Before long the water ran out. Hagar left her son lying under a bush, out of the sun.

decisions.choice: cast (hishlikh): put down quickly
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to throw (37:22). Here it describes Hagar setting the exhausted boy down in haste and despair, perhaps after supporting him.

decisions.choice: laid down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'laid down', since 'threw' would suggest violence (m1).

decisions.choice: out of the sun
decisions.reason: The point of putting him under a bush is shade from the sun; Readable says so.

records.source: וַתֵּלֶךְ֩ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב לָ֜הּ מִנֶּ֗גֶד הַרְחֵק֙ כִּמְטַחֲוֵ֣י קֶ֔שֶׁת כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֔ה אַל־אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּמ֣וֹת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־קֹלָ֖הּ וַתֵּֽבְךְּ׃
records.gloss: And she went and sat down by herself opposite, at a distance like shooters of a bow, for she said, let me not look on the death of the boy. And she sat opposite, and lifted up her voice and wept.
pieces: She moved away and sat down across from him at about the distance an arrow flies. "I will not watch while the boy dies," she said to herself. There she sat, facing him from a distance, and she wept aloud.

L.16: And she went and sat down by herself opposite [him], a good way off, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not look on the death of the child." And she sat opposite [him], and lifted up her voice and wept.

R.16: Then she went and sat down a long way off, about as far as someone can shoot an arrow. She thought, "I will not look while the boy is dying." And she sat there crying loudly.

decisions.choice: about a bowshot away: near enough to see, far enough not to watch
decisions.reason: The distance an arrow carries, perhaps a hundred yards or more. The bow anticipates what Ishmael will become (verse 20).

decisions.choice: she said: she said to herself
decisions.reason: As often, 'said' means thought (20:11).

decisions.choice: she lifted up her voice and wept: the Septuagint has 'the child'
alternatives: and the child lifted up his voice and wept
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint reads 'and the child cried aloud and wept', which fits verse 17, 'God heard the voice of the boy'. The Hebrew text, followed here, has Hagar weep.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַנַּעַר֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀אֶל־הָגָר֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ מַה־לָּ֣ךְ הָגָ֑ר אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא־שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And heard God the voice of the lad, and called [the] angel of God to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, what [is] to you, Hagar? Do not fear, for has heard God [the] voice of the lad where he [is] there.
pieces: God heard the boy's voice, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. "What is wrong, Hagar?" he said. "Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy's voice there where he lies.

L.17: And God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.

R.17: God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. He said, "Hagar, what is the matter? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy's cries from the place where he is.

decisions.choice: God heard: the meaning of Ishmael's name
decisions.reason: Ishmael means 'God hears' (16:11). Hagar wept, yet the text says that God heard the boy. Before he was born, God had heard his mother (16:11); now he hears the son.

decisions.choice: the angel of God called from heaven
decisions.reason: In chapter 16 the angel met Hagar on the road; here he calls from heaven, as he will call to Abraham in 22:11. The angel speaks for God and as God (verse 18, 'I will make him').

decisions.choice: where he is: as he is, where he lies
decisions.reason: God heard the boy in his present helpless state, where Hagar had left him.

decisions.choice: crying ... cries
decisions.reason: Readable says what the boy's 'voice' was: crying out in distress.

records.source: ק֚וּמִי שְׂאִ֣י אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר וְהַחֲזִ֥יקִי אֶת־יָדֵ֖ךְ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִׂימֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Arise, lift up the lad and hold your hand on him, for into a great nation I will make him.
pieces: Get up, raise the boy to his feet and take him firmly by the hand. I will make a great nation of him."

L.18: Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him fast with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation."

R.18: Get up! Go and lift the boy up, and hold his hand. I will make him the father of a great nation."

decisions.choice: I will make him a great nation: the angel speaks as God
decisions.reason: The angel speaks in God's own voice. The promise is to 'make him' a great nation, as with Abraham himself (12:2).

decisions.choice: hold him fast with your hand: support and take charge of him
decisions.reason: The phrase means to grip firmly; Hagar is to hold on to the boy and take him forward.

decisions.choice: the father of
decisions.reason: A man becomes a nation through his descendants; Readable says so.

records.source: וַיִּפְקַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא בְּאֵ֣ר מָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּ֤א אֶת־הַחֵ֨מֶת֙ מַ֔יִם וַתַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־הַנָּֽעַר׃
records.gloss: And opened God her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went and filled the skin [with] water and gave the lad a drink.
pieces: God opened her eyes, and there she saw a well. She went over, filled the skin and gave the boy water to drink.

L.19: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

R.19: Then God helped Hagar see a well nearby. She went and filled the bag with water and gave some to the boy.

decisions.choice: God opened her eyes: let her see what she had not seen
decisions.reason: The well may have been there all along; God makes her see it (2 Kings 6:17). In 16:13 Hagar named God 'the God who sees'; here he makes her see.

records.source: וַיְהִ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הַנַּ֖עַר וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיְהִ֖י רֹבֶ֥ה קַשָּֽׁת׃
records.gloss: And was God with the lad, and he grew up and dwelt in the wilderness and became a shooter, an archer.
pieces: God stayed with the boy while he grew. He settled in the wilderness and became an expert with the bow.

L.20: And God was with the boy, and he grew up; and he lived in the wilderness and became an archer, a bowman.

R.20: God took care of the boy as he grew. He made his home in the desert and became very good with a bow and arrows.

decisions.choice: God was with the boy: God's care continues
decisions.reason: 'God was with' someone means he protected and prospered them, as later with Isaac and Joseph (26:3; 39:2). The son sent away is not outside God's care.

decisions.choice: an archer, a bowman: a skilled hunter
decisions.reason: The exact sense of the first word (roveh) is uncertain, but the phrase means a skilled bowman. Esau, another son who does not carry the promise, is also a hunter (25:27).

records.source: וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר פָּארָ֑ן וַתִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ אִמּ֛וֹ אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: And he dwelt in [the] wilderness of Paran, and took for him his mother a wife from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: He made his home in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother found him a wife from Egypt.

L.21: And he lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

R.21: He lived in the Desert of Paran. His mother chose a wife for him from Egypt, her homeland.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Paran: the desert south of Canaan
decisions.reason: Paran is the desert region in the north of the Sinai Peninsula, where Israel later wandered (Numbers 10:12; 12:16).

decisions.choice: his mother took a wife for him: an arranged marriage
decisions.reason: Parents arranged marriages. Hagar, an Egyptian (16:1), finds a wife for her son from her own people, as Abraham will find one for Isaac from his own family (24:3-4).

decisions.choice: her homeland
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that Hagar came from Egypt (16:1).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עִמְּךָ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And it was at that time, and said Abimelech and Phicol, [the] commander of his army, to Abraham, saying, God [is] with you in all that you are doing.
pieces: Around that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham: "God is with you in whatever you do.

L.22: And at that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, "God is with you in all that you do.

R.22: At that time Abimelech came to Abraham with Phicol, the commander of his army. Abimelech said, "We can see that God is with you in everything you do.

decisions.choice: God is with you: outsiders see the blessing
decisions.reason: The words that have just been said of Ishmael (verse 20) are said of Abraham by a foreign king, who has seen God's protection of him (chapter 20). He comes as one seeking a treaty with a stronger party. In 26:28 Abimelech says the same of Isaac.

decisions.choice: Phicol: a name of unknown meaning
decisions.reason: The name may not be Semitic. The commander of the army comes because a treaty between powers is a matter of security.

decisions.choice: We can see that
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Abimelech speaks from what he has observed.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֨בְעָה לִּ֤י בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה אִם־תִּשְׁקֹ֣ר לִ֔י וּלְנִינִ֖י וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י כַּחֶ֜סֶד אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֤יתִי עִמְּךָ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עִמָּדִ֔י וְעִם־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־גַּ֥רְתָּה בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And now swear to me by God here that you will not deal falsely with me and with my offspring and with my posterity; according to the kindness that I have done with you, you will do with me and with the land in which you have sojourned.
pieces: So swear to me by God, here and now, that you will never play me false, nor my children, nor their descendants after them. I have kept faith with you; keep faith in the same way with me and with this land where you have made your home as a foreigner."

L.23: And now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my children or with my descendants, but as I have shown kindness to you, you will show [it] to me and to the land in which you have sojourned."

R.23: So promise me here, with God as your witness, that you will not trick me or my children or my grandchildren. I have been kind to you. Be kind to me in the same way, and to this country where you have been living as an outsider."

decisions.choice: swear by God: an oath with God as witness
decisions.reason: An oath called on God to witness the promise and to punish the one who broke it. The name of the place, Beersheba, will come from this oath (verse 31).

decisions.choice: my children and my descendants (nin, neked): all who come after me
decisions.reason: The two words are a fixed pair for a man's line of descendants (Job 18:19; Isaiah 14:22). Abimelech wants a treaty that will last for generations.

decisions.choice: kindness (chesed): loyalty under an agreement
decisions.reason: The same word as in 20:13: the faithful conduct owed within a relationship. Abimelech had treated Abraham generously (20:14-15) and asks for the same in return.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אָנֹכִ֖י אִשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: And said Abraham, I will swear.
pieces: Abraham replied, "I give you my oath."

R.24: Abraham said, "I will swear to it."

records.source: וְהוֹכִ֥חַ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ עַל־אֹדוֹת֙ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּזְל֖וּ עַבְדֵ֥י אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And reproved Abraham Abimelech on account of the well of water which had seized [the] servants of Abimelech.
pieces: Abraham, however, took Abimelech to task over a well that Abimelech's men had taken from him by force.

L.25: And Abraham reproved Abimelech about the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.

R.25: But Abraham had a complaint against Abimelech. Abimelech's men had taken over one of Abraham's wells.

decisions.choice: reproved (hokhiach): raised a complaint
decisions.reason: The verb means to argue a case or call someone to account. Before the oath is sworn, Abraham brings up a wrong that must be put right.

decisions.choice: the well: water rights in a dry land
decisions.reason: In the Negev a well meant life for flocks and herds, and wells were fought over (26:15-22). Whoever dug a well claimed the right to it.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: The word (eved) may mean slaves or a king's officers; Balanced and Readable say 'men', since the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: one of Abraham's wells
decisions.reason: Readable says whose well it was; verse 30 shows Abraham had dug it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְגַם־אַתָּ֞ה לֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֗י וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בִּלְתִּ֥י הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And said Abimelech, I do not know who has done this thing; and also you did not tell me, and also I did not hear except today.
pieces: Abimelech said, "I have no idea who did this. You never told me, and this is the first I have heard of it."

L.26: And Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this thing. You did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today."

R.26: Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this. You never told me about it. This is the first time I have heard of it."

decisions.choice: you did not tell me, and I did not hear: a threefold denial
decisions.reason: Three times Abimelech says 'not': he did not know, Abraham did not tell, he did not hear. He clears himself of the wrong and implies that Abraham should have spoken sooner.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: And took Abraham sheep and cattle and gave [them] to Abimelech, and made the two of them a covenant.
pieces: Abraham then presented Abimelech with sheep and cattle, and the two of them entered into a covenant.

L.27: And Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave [them] to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.

R.27: Then Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, and the two of them made a covenant with each other.

decisions.choice: made a covenant: literally 'cut a covenant'
decisions.reason: The verb (karat) means 'cut', perhaps from the animals cut in two when a covenant was made (15:9-18). A covenant here is a sworn treaty between two parties.

decisions.choice: Abraham gave sheep and cattle: gifts that seal the treaty
decisions.reason: As Abimelech had given gifts to Abraham (20:14), Abraham now gives to him; the gifts confirm the agreement.

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֣ב אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶת־שֶׁ֛בַע כִּבְשֹׂ֥ת הַצֹּ֖אן לְבַדְּהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And set Abraham seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
pieces: Then Abraham took seven young ewes from the flock and placed them to one side.

L.28: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart by themselves.

R.28: Abraham also took seven female lambs from his flock and put them off by themselves.

decisions.choice: seven (sheva): a play on 'oath'
decisions.reason: The Hebrew for 'seven' (sheva) sounds like the verb 'swear' (nishba). The seven lambs and the oath together give the place its name (verse 31).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֑ם מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה שֶׁ֤בַע כְּבָשֹׂת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצַּ֖בְתָּ לְבַדָּֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And said Abimelech to Abraham, what [are] these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?
pieces: Abimelech asked Abraham, "Why have you put these seven lambs off to one side?"

L.29: And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What are these seven ewe lambs here that you have set by themselves?"

R.29: Abimelech asked, "What are these seven lambs for? Why did you put them by themselves?"

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֚י אֶת־שֶׁ֣בַע כְּבָשֹׂ֔ת תִּקַּ֖ח מִיָּדִ֑י בַּעֲבוּר֙ תִּֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣י לְעֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י חָפַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־הַבְּאֵ֥ר הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And he said, for the seven ewe lambs you will take from my hand, so that it will be for me a witness that I dug this well.
pieces: He answered, "Take these seven lambs from me. They will stand as my proof that I am the one who dug this well."

L.30: And he said, "These seven ewe lambs you shall take from my hand, so that it may be a witness for me that I dug this well."

R.30: Abraham answered, "Take these seven lambs from me. Then everyone will know that I dug this well and that it belongs to me."

decisions.choice: you shall take from my hand ... a witness: accepting the gift accepts the claim
decisions.reason: By accepting the lambs in front of witnesses, Abimelech would publicly recognize that the well belonged to Abraham. Ownership was confirmed by a public act, not by a written deed.

decisions.choice: and that it belongs to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the proof was for: Abraham's right to the well.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ם נִשְׁבְּע֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore he called the place that Beersheba, for there swore the two of them.
pieces: That is why the place was named Beersheba: the two of them took an oath there.

L.31: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, for there the two of them swore.

R.31: So that place was called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath" or "well of seven." It got that name because the two men made a solemn promise to each other there.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: 'well of the oath' or 'well of seven'
decisions.reason: Beer means well, and sheba can mean both 'seven' and 'oath'. The name recalls the seven lambs (verses 28-30) and the oath (verse 31). Isaac later renews the name (26:33).

decisions.choice: which means "well of the oath" or "well of seven"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name so the reason given makes sense (m1).

records.source: וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיָּ֣קָם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And they made a covenant at Beersheba; and arose Abimelech and Phicol, [the] commander of his army, and returned to [the] land of [the] Philistines.
pieces: Once the covenant at Beersheba was made, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol got up and went home to the land of the Philistines.

L.32: So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army rose and returned to the land of the Philistines.

R.32: When the covenant was made at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol left. They returned to the land of the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines: the coastal region later known by that name
decisions.reason: The Philistines best known in the Bible settled on the southern coast around 1200 BC, long after Abraham's day. The narrator uses the name by which the region and its people were later known; it may also refer to an earlier group of the same name (26:1).

records.source: וַיִּטַּ֥ע אֶ֖שֶׁל בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּ֨קְרָא־שָׁ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֵ֥ל עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he planted a tamarisk in Beersheba, and called there on [the] name of YHWH, God of eternity.
pieces: Abraham planted a tamarisk at Beersheba. There he worshiped, calling on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God Everlasting.

L.33: And he planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and called there on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Everlasting God.

R.33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who lives forever.

decisions.choice: a tamarisk: a hardy desert tree
decisions.reason: The tamarisk grows in dry ground and gives shade for many years. Planting one was a sign that Abraham meant to stay; trees often marked places of worship and meeting (12:6; 1 Samuel 22:6).

decisions.choice: the Everlasting God (El Olam)
decisions.reason: Olam means a time without limit. Abraham names the LORD as the God who lasts forever (Isaiah 40:28), beside a treaty meant to last for generations (verse 23).

decisions.choice: called on the name of the LORD: worshiped
decisions.reason: To call on God's name is to pray to him and worship him (4:26; 12:8; 26:25).

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: The subject is supplied; the Hebrew says 'he'.

decisions.choice: worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m3).

records.source: וַיָּ֧גָר אַבְרָהָ֛ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And sojourned Abraham in [the] land of [the] Philistines many days.
pieces: For a long time after that, Abraham lived as a resident foreigner in the land of the Philistines.

L.34: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

R.34: Abraham stayed on in the land of the Philistines for a long time, living there as an outsider.

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as a foreigner
decisions.reason: Even with a well and a treaty, Abraham remains a resident foreigner in the land promised to his descendants (20:1; 23:4).
